chunks: From him, from Safwan, from Abd Allah ibn Muskān, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Ziyād, from Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about the freed slave (mamlūk), what is permissible for him from women? He said: Two free women or four slave women. He said: And there is no objection if his master permits him to buy from his own wealth, if he has wealth, a female slave or female slaves whom he may have intercourse with, and his slave women are permissible for him.

key_terms.الْمَمْلُوكِ: A slave who has been freed but still owes a portion of his value to his master

ai.seo_question: What are the marriage options for a partially freed slave (mamlūk) in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Istibsar clarifies the specific marital capacity of a mamlūk, distinguishing his right to contract marriage with two free women or four slave women based on his financial independence. It further establishes that with the master's permission, a mamlūk may purchase a female slave using his own accumulated wealth (mal), thereby integrating her into his permissible sphere of union. This ruling highlights the nuanced legal status of the mamlūk in Shia jurisprudence, balancing his partial freedom with the master's residual rights.
